topic: Configure youtube-transcript skill: yt-dlp primary, better infra fit
initialPrompt:
Check out C:\Users\intel\DevelopmentProjectTemplate\.agents\skills\youtube-transcript

Lets configure this skill to my preference, and work better with my infracstructure, and also lets make it mainly rely on ytdlp instead of the deepai api. Also im not too knowledgeable about ytdlp, is there some kinda setup we need to do for it too work?

qAndA.question: Self-resolved: The skill's json3->txt flattener must not use 'python3' — on this machine 'python3' resolves to the WindowsApps Store stub (verified symlink to AppInstallerPythonRedirector), which would break the skill. 'python' resolves to real Python 3.14.6. Since the project's skill-script convention is Node.js (log-session, grill-me-v3 both use Node helpers, node v24.18.0 present), the rewritten skill gets a scripts/ dir with a Node-based flattener.

Self-resolved: ffmpeg is NOT required for transcript extraction (yt-dlp --skip-download --write-subs writes subtitle files directly, no muxing). ffmpeg is only needed for the audio/Whisper path, which stays out of scope unless the user explicitly asks. No ffmpeg setup needed.
Self-resolved: deno is NOT required — node v24.18.0 is on PATH, which satisfies yt-dlp's JS-runtime needs for YouTube extraction in newer versions. Will verify empirically after install.

Self-resolved: keep en.* as default subtitle languages with the --list-subs fallback for non-English videos; keep Channel_Title file naming (fall back to video ID); keep 'report saved path, print text if short, never report costs unless asked' output convention.

Self-resolved: 429 / 'Sign in to confirm you're not a bot' = IP flagged. NEVER loop retries (makes it worse). Stop, tell the user, and offer the browser-cookies mitigation — never auto-crank retries. This stays a hard rule in the rewritten skill.

Q1 — yt-dlp install method: yt-dlp is NOT installed on this machine, so yes — setup is required. How do you want it installed? (a) pip install into Python 3.14 (recommended — official distribution, self-updates via 'yt-dlp -U', lands in Python314/Scripts which is already on PATH), (b) scoop install yt-dlp (you already use scoop for opencode/rage; keeps Python out of it), or (c) winget install yt-dlp. All three put 'yt-dlp' on PATH so the skill works identically either way — this is about how you prefer to manage system tools on this machine.
qAndA.answer: lets do a, but lets turn off self updates

qAndA.question: Self-resolved (from Q1 answer): self-updates OFF. The rewritten skill will never run 'yt-dlp -U' or any auto-update. Failure handling becomes: retry once (no update), then stop and report. Updates happen only manually, on the user's say-so, via 'pip install -U yt-dlp'. (This also sidesteps the pip-install quirk where 'yt-dlp -U' doesn't work for pip-installed copies.)

Q2 — DeepAPI fate: there is no DeepAPI key on this machine (~/.deepapi missing, DEEPAPI_API_KEY nowhere in the repo) — the current 'primary' path has never actually run here. You said the skill should 'mainly rely on ytdlp instead of the deepai api'. Do you have a deepapi.co account/key at all? (a) No account → drop DeepAPI entirely; pure yt-dlp skill, one true path, much simpler (recommended if you don't have a key). (b) Yes, I have/plan a key → keep DeepAPI as a clearly-marked optional secondary section that only activates if ~/.deepapi/env exists.
qAndA.answer: there is no deep api, drop deep api entirely

qAndA.question: Q3 — Save location for transcript files: the current skill saves to the project/working dir if it makes sense, else ~/Downloads (which on this machine is a cluttered catch-all). Where should transcripts land? (a) Keep current behavior — cwd when it makes sense, else ~/Downloads (recommended: flexible, matches how you use other skills). (b) Always ~/Downloads — one predictable place, but easy to lose in the clutter. (c) A dedicated transcripts folder, e.g. ~/Downloads/transcripts — keeps transcripts grouped and out of the way.

Q4 — Bot-flag (429 / 'Sign in to confirm you're not a bot') policy: this is exactly the failure mode DeepAPI was originally chosen to dodge — your home IP can get flagged by YouTube. yt-dlp is now primary, so this WILL happen occasionally. When it does: (a) Plain — stop, tell you, done, no cookie tricks. (b) Auto-fallback — on 429/bot-flag, try once with --cookies-from-browser (your installed browsers: Chrome/Vivaldi/Edge), then stop and report (recommended: this is the single most effective fix, and cookie-bypassed requests often succeed where anonymous ones fail). (c) On-demand only — plain by default; only reach for browser cookies when you explicitly say so.

Self-resolved (from Q4 answer): cookies fallback chain — on 429/bot-flag, attempt --cookies-from-browser exactly once per browser in a sensible order (chrome, then vivaldi, then edge, skipping any that error), then stop and report. The skill notes the caveat that a running browser may lock its cookie DB; if the first browser fails, try the next.

User directive (logged): 'Honestly lets go ahead and just make these edits you dont even gotta close off. Lets get to work on this now.' — explicit authorization to implement the configured youtube-transcript skill rewrite now. Session log left active per the user's request (no close ceremony).

DECISION REVISED (empirical evidence overrides #3): live testing showed yt-dlp 2026.07 only enables deno by default — 'No supported JavaScript runtime could be found... to use another runtime add --js-runtimes RUNTIME'. Node does NOT auto-cover extraction. Verified fix: add '--js-runtimes node' to every yt-dlp command (node v24.18.0 on PATH). Logged as a revision of decision #3.

New self-resolved decision (from live testing): install curl_cffi (pip) so yt-dlp can impersonate a browser — the youtube extractor warned 'impersonation requested but no impersonate target available'. curl_cffi directly reduces the 429/bot-flag risk agreed in Q4. Verified the warning disappears with it installed. Documented as recommended setup alongside yt-dlp.

New self-resolved decision (from live testing): the original '--sub-langs en.*' pattern is dangerous — live test grabbed native en.json3 THEN translations (en-ar, en-bg...) and triggered HTTP 429 mid-burst. Verified '--sub-langs "en,en-orig"' matches EXACTLY (native manual en, native auto en-orig, no translations, no burst). --list-subs fallback section covers en-US/non-English videos.

New self-resolved decision (from live testing): add '--sleep-requests 1' (pace extraction requests) and '--no-playlist' (never expand playlist/channel URLs into bulk downloads) to all yt-dlp commands; flatten explicitly to '$OUT/$NAME.txt' (clean Channel_Title.txt naming instead of inheriting .en from the json3).

DECISION CORRECTED (evidence overrides #14): curl_cffi 0.16.0 (latest available for Python 3.14/3.12) is marked '(unsupported)' by yt-dlp 2026.07.04 — impersonation targets remain unavailable and '--impersonate chrome' hard-errors. Final call: keep curl_cffi installed (harmless, may light up when yt-dlp supports this version) but do NOT include --impersonate in the skill. The impersonation warning is benign for caption downloads; skill notes to ignore ffmpeg/impersonation warnings.

New self-resolved decision (from user's edge-case question): added a pre-flight guard to the skill's main flow — 'command -v yt-dlp' and 'command -v node' checks that fail loudly with install instructions instead of the previous misleading 'Could not fetch video metadata — check the URL' (the missing-binary error was being swallowed by 2>/dev/null on the metadata call). Deliberately NO auto-install — consistent with the user's manual-update preference.

User directive (logged): 'Plan out any other potential edge cases we could run into for this skill real quick. dont implement or execute any fixes or anything though.' — edge-case plan delivered in-session, NO fixes implemented. Findings summarized: 8 would-fix gaps (429-on-metadata falls to misleading error, 403 not covered, misleading no-captions message when non-English subs exist, Windows long-title truncation, cwd-anchoring of OUT, empty/corrupt json3 silently writes empty txt, outdated-yt-dlp hint, partial non-ASCII title mangling) + 3 scope flags (playlist URLs take first video only, yt-dlp supports non-YouTube sites, timestamped output unavailable).
